title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 108
paragraphs: Meanwhile, while the news about Sardis was going up to the king, and while Darius, after doing what he did with the bow, was coming to speech with Histiaeus, and Histiaeus, having been let go by Darius, was making his way to the coast—during all this time the following events were taking place. As Onesilus of Salamis was besieging those of Amathus, it was reported to him that Artybius, a Persian, bringing with him on ships a large Persian army, was expected soon to arrive in Cyprus. On receiving this news, Onesilus sent heralds to various places in Ionia to summon the Ionians to his aid; and they took counsel together and came without delay with a large force. The Ionians arrived in Cyprus just at the time when the Persians, having crossed over from Cilicia in ships, were proceeding by land to attack Salamis, while the Phoenicians with the ships were sailing around the headland called the “Keys of Cyprus.”
